artifacts.summary: Measured the full 95-suite shell test suite for the first time (~650s / ~10m sequential). Found test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh alone costs 391s (60% of total) via 4 real full-gate-battery verify-deploy.sh invocations, dwarfing the dispatch's named example (test-force-phases.sh, 5.39s, 0.8% of total). Recommends prioritizing a verify-deploy.sh gate-selection flag first, then file-level parallelism, then targeted in-process extraction, with fixture-reuse/file-splitting lowest priority. Also documents a pre-existing intermittent flake and 4 pre-existing unrelated failures for baseline verification purposes.

memory_candidates.content: When measuring shell-test-suite performance, do not assume the file with the most subprocess invocations (highest 'amplification' count) dominates wall time. In this repo, a 530-line file with 46 subprocess calls cost 5.4s (0.8% of a ~650s suite) while a 261-line file cost 391s (60%) because it invoked a full ~20-gate verify script 4 times instead of a single targeted gate. Always measure per-file wall time directly (instrument the suite runner's own discovery loop with date +%s%N around each invocation) before choosing an optimization target.

Bash process-startup and library-sourcing overhead is negligible in this codebase: bare `bash -c ':'` vs. sourcing a real ~200-line common.sh lib showed no measurable difference over 50 iterations (0.115s vs 0.119s), and jq-parsing a 1244-line real state.json took ~5ms. Test-suite slowness from 'process-spawn amplification' claims should be verified against actual per-call cost before assuming subprocess count alone explains wall time -- the called script's own work (mutex locks, git operations, real multi-gate verification scripts) is almost always the actual cost driver, not shell startup.

test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (in this repo's core test suite) demonstrates a reusable pattern for de-amplifying tests that need to exercise orchestration logic without paying for the real heavy dependency: it writes a small call-counting stub script into the fixture's .claude/scripts/ in place of the real verify-deploy.sh, and asserts on stub-call counts (e.g. 'verify-deploy.sh called exactly once') rather than invoking the real ~100s-per-call gate battery. Worth reusing as a template whenever a test needs call-count assertions against an expensive real script it doesn't need to fully execute.
